items.reason: The lift field flows through build options into row lifting and marking.
Only the shipped active preset enables Lift.
pin silently decodes into the same Lift field.
lift is decoded after pin and overrides its boolean value.
An omitted grant defaults to false.
Both spellings record non-boolean values as findings without failing loading.
Derived-ordering identifiers, comments and affected test filenames are renamed to lift.
The specified manual and unrelated pin meanings remain unchanged.
The field metadata and shipped presets use lift; pin remains a decoding alias.
Repository attribution reaches sets from sibling worktrees, with integration coverage.
Checkout attribution returns before the repository pass and retains its existing ranking.
Task-set tags retain precedence over checkout and repository answers.
Repository candidates include both bound and unbound Task sets.
ID-only attribution indexes and project-name-based cursor keys still collide across repositories sharing project names and container IDs, allowing incorrect lifting.
Missing or unknown repositories produce no attribution, lifting or status message.
The repository pass concatenates kind answers, explicitly tested with two answering kinds.
Launch resolves the repository once; a counting git seam checks ten subsequent rebuilds.
Status uses empty pane facts, with tests asserting no lifting or attribution git calls.
Lifting only moves admitted rows and preserves preset narrowing.
Map locality includes active and arrived Maps while excluding abandoned and broken Maps.
Integration coverage asserts Task sets and Maps lift together, with sets first.
Map session stamps retain precedence, with a repository-fallback regression test.
Routines implement no locality attribution, and comments explicitly explain the asymmetry.

scores.rationale: Clear seams and substantial regression coverage, but repository identity collisions remain untested and violate isolation; assessment is static because the supplied diff is unapplied.

accepted.behaviour: The repository pass matches a pane to work by the repository's git common directory, not by project name, so a sibling worktree matches and two repositories that share a project name do not share work.
accepted.reason: The spec (spec.md:107-110) makes the git common directory the repository identity and rejects the project name because two repositories can collide on it. The Reference matches by the common directory, but it lifts the row by a cursor key made from the project name and the container ID. So two repositories with the same project name and the same container ID can lift each other's row. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.
